# F-016 C1 live check (~2.5 minutes). Expect: each scene on the whole slide, the title floating top left; a boy clearly
# taller than the book in his hand; a dog on a grey moon with a cat on it (one dog, the same scene); "back to the slide"
# (singular) ends it; a sphere inside a see-through cuboid; you inside a rocket in space and the sun; a bird on a tree
# and its feet in a magnifier; the bus brakes and you lean forward, then the camera on you; Imagine Mode (pressed by
# @command): a laptop on a flying airplane, a fish near a bicycle under the ocean, then End -> one recap.
@setup subject=Physics grade=9 topic="Imagination"

Today we will imagine a few scenes.
[pause 1]
Imagine a boy holding a book.
[pause 3]
Imagine a dog on the moon.
[pause 3]
Now a cat sits on top of the dog.
[pause 3]
Let's get back to the slide.
[pause 1.5]
Imagine a cuboid with a sphere inside it.
[pause 3]
Back to the slides.
[pause 1.5]
Imagine you are in a rocket going to the sun.
[pause 3.5]
Imagine a bird on a tree.
[pause 3]
Look at its feet.
[pause 3]
Back to the slides.
[pause 1.5]
Imagine you're on a bus and it brakes.
[pause 3.5]
Look at the person inside.
[pause 3]
Back to the slides.
[pause 1.5]
@command imagine_mode on=true
A laptop is flying on top of an airplane.
[pause 3]
So what do you think?
[pause 2]
A fish swims under the ocean near a bicycle.
[pause 3.5]
@command imagine_mode on=false
[pause 1]
That is how imagination helps us picture physics.
